candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a rare WHO grade II neuronal-glial tumor with lipomatous differentiation. Medulloblastoma is a high-grade (WHO grade IV) embryonal tumor. Although both can present as midline cerebellar vermis masses with similar MRI features (T2 heterogeneity, restricted diffusion, enhancement), the patient's age (44 years), the 4-month indolent course, and the specific imaging characteristics (heterogeneous T2 signal without surrounding edema, no hemorrhage/calcification on GRE) are more consistent with liponeurocytoma. Medulloblastoma is a related but incompatible subtype—it is a different tumor class, not an alias or parent of liponeurocytoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Medulloblastoma is a distinct WHO-classified embryonal tumor of the cerebellum, not a liponeurocytoma; both arise in the cerebellar vermis and share some imaging overlap, but they are separate diagnostic entities with different histology, prognosis, and management

case_quality_flags: Liponeurocytoma is a very rare entity; restricted diffusion and elevated choline on MRS can mimic medulloblastoma, making histopathological confirmation essential
Patient age (44 years) strongly favors liponeurocytoma over medulloblastoma, which peaks in childhood/young adulthood
